Subject: Acme rehearsal recap + next steps (owners & timing)

Hi Elaine / Tom —

Thanks again for running the rehearsal on Tue. Quick recap and clear next steps so nothing falls through the cracks:

What we ran
- Prompt workshop (20m): reviewed 12 sample prompts and agreed on two routing tiers: low-latency (q1) and high-fidelity (q2). I attached the prompt sets we used.
- Load test (30m): Ben executed the controlled burst schedule (50 rps peak, gradual ramp). No errors observed; 95th latency stayed within the SLA for q1 routing.
- Connectivity check (10m): SRE confirmed firewall rules and IP allowlist. Procurement confirmed PoA receipt.

Open items / owners (with target dates)
- Finalize routing map and export to your engineering team (owner: Marissa Cole) — target 2027-12-13
- Share sanitized session logs and token-cost estimate for typical traffic (owner: Ben Carter) — target 2027-12-10 (attached session_log_20271206.txt)
- Procurement: sign the SOW via DocuSign (owner: Acme procurement) — target 2027-12-12
- Follow-up hands-on: 90m working session to validate edge-case prompts and A/B routing behavior (proposed window: week of Dec 20) — Diego to propose 3 slots by EOD 2027-12-09

Notes:
- We recommend enabling short-term prefix caching for a sample of high-frequency prompts to lower repeated-token costs; I'll include quantization recommendations in the routing doc.
- Ben flagged one prompt that caused unusually long generation (attached note in session log). We'll re-run that prompt in isolation during the follow-up session.

Attachments included: redwood_acme_rehearsal_agenda.pdf, session_log_20271206.txt

Next steps: Diego will send the calendar proposal for the Dec 20 window, and Ben/Marissa will deliver the two deliverables above. If you prefer the follow-up earlier, let us know and we'll compress timelines.

Appreciate the collaboration — see you soon.

— Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
